lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: the correlation coefficient, slope and intercept in context, and correlation versus causation

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales correlate with drowning rates. Does ice cream cause drowning?

steps: A lurking variable explains the association.
workedSolution.answer: No; a third variable explains it

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set records 19, 6, 16, 12, 6. Give the mean and the median.
A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 183 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 33 yes, 58 no; row 2: 40 yes, 10 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 16x + 58, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 16 test points.
Each additional test points is associated with 16 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 16 test points.
The predicted value is 16 test points when x is 0.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
